items.title: Intensive early and sustained lowering of LDL-C and inflammation after index PCI and cardiovascular outcomes.
items.abstract: Atherogenic dyslipidemia and inflammation are associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, yet the relationship between their target achievement patterns and cardiovascular outcomes remains unclear. Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels were measured at admission, 2 months, and 1 year after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as the composite of non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, cardiovascular death, and unplanned revascularization. Four target achievement patterns were defined based on whether LDL-C and CRP targets were reached at 2 months and 1 year. The association between LDL-C and CRP levels, target achievement patterns and outcomes were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic splines. During a median follow-up of 714 days, 505 patients experienced MACE. Early and sustained achievement of LDL-C or CRP targets was individually associated with the lowest risk of MACE compared to those who never achieved the respective targets (HR = 0.600, 95% CI 0.448 - 0.805; HR = 0.688, 95% CI 0.489 - 0.970, respectively). Moreover, the combined effect of achieving early and sustained targets for both LDL-C and CRP was associated with the greatest reduction in MACE risk (HR = 0.539, 95% CI 0.387 - 0.752). Early and sustained target achievement patterns of both LDL-C and CRP after index PCI are associated with a significantly lower risk of MACE. These findings support the early initiation and long-term maintenance of combined lipid-lowering and anti-inflammatory strategies to optimize outcomes in post-PCI patients.

items.title: Association between plasma long-chain acylcarnitines and long-term mortality and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with coronary artery disease.
items.abstract: We assessed whether baseline circulating long-chain acylcarnitine levels were associated with increased risk of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with suspected or established coronary artery disease (CAD). We measured four previously identified high-risk plasma acylcarnitine species (i.e., C14:0, C14:1, C16:0, and C16:1) in 167 consecutive Italian patients who underwent urgent or elective coronary angiography for suspected or established CAD in 2017 (at baseline) and were followed for a median of 84.1 months (interquartile range: 81.8-85.2 months). Baseline plasma acylcarnitine species were quantified by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality or incident nonfatal cardiovascular events (acute myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or permanent atrial fibrillation). During the follow-up, 50 events occurred (31 of which were deaths). Higher baseline circulating levels of acylcarnitine C14:0 (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] per 1-SD increase 1.44, 95%CI 1.15-1.82; p = 0.002), acylcarnitine C14:1 (aHR 1.26, 95%CI 1.01-1.57; p = 0.045), acylcarnitine C16:0 (aHR 1.38, 95%CI 1.07-1.77; p = 0.014), and acylcarnitine C16:1 (aHR 1.40, 95%CI 1.10-1.79; p = 0.006) were associated with a higher risk of the primary composite outcome, independent of age, sex, diabetes status, prior CAD history and lipid-lowering medication use. We observed similar results for all-cause mortality as the outcome. These associations remained significant even after Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple testing. Among patients undergoing coronary angiography for suspected or established CAD, higher baseline plasma long-chain acylcarnitine levels were independently associated with worse long-term prognosis, irrespective of traditional cardiovascular risk factors.

items.title: Corrigendum to "Urinary tract and genital infections with dapagliflozin and empagliflozin across type 2 diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease: An indication- and sex-stratified disproportionality analysis of eudravigilance reports" [Biomed. Pharmacother. 204 (2026) 119976].
Severe maternal morbidity in patients with cardiovascular disease and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are independently associated with increased risk of severe maternal morbidity (SMM). While prior studies have characterized adverse pregnancy outcomes among patients with CVD, limited data have evaluated how the development of HDP influences non-transfusion SMM across specific cardiac subtypes, particularly through the postpartum period, in large contemporary U.S. cohorts. To assess the impact of HDP on non-transfusion SMM among patients with CVD during delivery and within 90 days postpartum. Retrospective cohort study using the Premier Healthcare Database of pregnant patients ≥18 years delivering between 2015 and 2020. Patients without CVD were compared to those with six CVD subtypes present on admission (aortic, ischemic, congenital, pulmonary hypertension, cardiomyopathy, and valvular). The primary outcome was non-transfusion SMM during delivery hospitalization and within 90 days postpartum, stratified by CVD and HDP subtype (gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, and preeclampsia with severe features), estimated as covariate-adjusted predicted rates (%). Secondary outcomes included SMM subtypes, ICU admission, and all-cause readmission within 30 and 90 days, reported as crude rates and adjusted odds ratios (aORs). Of 4,606,247 births, 18,771 (0.4%) had CVD, and 12.0% had HDP. HDP was associated with higher adjusted predicted non-transfusion SMM rates, independent of CVD, with increasing risk across HDP severity and marked heterogeneity by CVD subtype. Patients with CVD had consistently higher SMM across all HDP subtypes. The highest delivery hospitalization SMM rates occurred among patients with cardiomyopathy (25.6%) and pulmonary hypertension (33.2%) with preeclampsia with severe features; this pattern persisted through 90 days postpartum. Acute respiratory distress syndrome and mechanical ventilation were the most common SMM types during delivery, while heart failure/pulmonary edema predominated postpartum. Cardiomyopathy (aOR 9.02) and pulmonary hypertension (aOR 4.37) had the highest odds of ICU admission; readmission risk was also highest in pulmonary hypertension (30-day aOR 1.77; 90-day aOR 1.76) and cardiomyopathy (30-day aOR 1.42; 90-day aOR 1.68). HDP significantly increases risk of non-transfusion SMM in patients with CVD, particularly in pulmonary hypertension and cardiomyopathy, and in those with preeclampsia with severe features.

items.title: Germline pharmacogenomics of platinum, radiotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitor toxicity in non-small cell lung cancer: a mechanism-based systematic review and appraisal against CPIC evidence standards.
items.abstract: Germline variants predicting treatment toxicity guide care for a few drug-gene pairs, yet most reported associations never reach the clinic. Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) isolates the problem: somatic genotyping is standard and toxicity limits dose intensity across chemotherapy, radiotherapy and immunotherapy, yet no germline marker guides therapy. Per a registered protocol (PROSPERO CRD420261364865), we searched four databases for 2020-2026 publications, synthesizing 35 studies from 15 countries. Thirty-four variant-toxicity associations were grouped by mechanism (transport/metabolism, DNA repair, immune regulation, target pathway). The 11 priority loci (12 variants) were benchmarked against the Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium (CPIC) hierarchy. Twenty-nine of 34 associations were nominally significant. Of 10 studies correcting for multiplicity, seven had a finding that passed its own threshold (the lead association in five). Of 12 studies with validation analyses, three mounted an independent attempt (two with stated reservations), all nominally positive (single SNP, FDR-adjusted p=0.179; polygenic score; 27 patients); none replicated an association passing a multiplicity threshold. Across 23 significant lead associations, effect magnitude decreased with sample size (Spearman ρ=-0.48, 95% CI -0.81 to -0.07), consistent with selection-driven inflation. XRCC1 rs25487 effects differed by treatment and endpoint. No priority locus reached CPIC level A or B for its NSCLC drug pair. Many germline toxicity biomarkers are reported in NSCLC, but evidence remains exploratory: validation is uncommon, effect-size inflation is plausible, and within the review window no candidate met implementation standards. The bottleneck is evidence maturation, not discovery. We propose a four-phase framework toward genotype-guided care.

items.title: An ultrasound-triggered nanoplatform for enhanced sonodynamic immunotherapy achieved through Diels-Alder bond cleavage and in situ vaccine formation.
items.abstract: Sonodynamic immunotherapy (SIT) presents prominent potential in amplified therapy against malignant tumors due to its precise spatiotemporal controllability and systemic immune activation capability. However, achieving synergistic integration of sonodynamic therapy (SDT) and immunotherapy to maximize anti-tumor efficacy remains an urgent and critical challenge. Herein, we constructed an ultrasound-triggered nanoplatform (MRPT), where MRPT could generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) for SDT under ultrasound irradiation, while the Diels-Alder (D-A) bond was broken to release immunoadjuvant R837 and capture tumor-associated antigens (TAAs) as in-situ vaccine for enhanced SIT. The exposed Mal groups enabled efficient binding to sulfhydryl groups of TAAs, facilitating efficient antigen capture, where the amount of ovalbumin captured by MRPT was around 2.7-fold that without ultrasound. Benefiting from SDT-induced immunogenic cell death (ICD), R837-mediated immune-stimulation, as well as in-situ vaccine formed by captured TAAs, the proportion of mature dendritic cells (DCs) in the spleen significantly increased up to 40.6%, CD8 + T cell infiltration was promoted, and regulatory T cell (Treg) proportion was also greatly reduced. Thus, this strategy offers a promising avenue for enhanced SIT in malignant tumor treatment. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Sonodynamic immunotherapy offers a promising strategy for treating malignant tumors, yet its therapeutic efficacy is often limited by the insufficient coordination between sonodynamic therapy and immune activation. In this study, we developed an ultrasound-triggered MRPT nanoplatform that integrates reactive oxygen species generation, immunoadjuvant release, and tumor-associated antigen capture within a single system. Upon ultrasound irradiation, MRPT efficiently induced immunogenic cell death, released the immune agonist R837, and exposed maleimide groups for enhanced capture of tumor-associated antigens, with an approximately 2.7-fold increase in ovalbumin capture compared with the non-irradiated condition. This multifunctional design promoted dendritic-cell maturation, enhanced CD8 + T-cell infiltration, and reduced regulatory T-cell proportions, thereby remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment. These findings demonstrate that ultrasound-regulated antigen capture and immune stimulation can effectively strengthen sonodynamic immunotherapy and provide a promising platform for developing more potent tumor vaccines and systemic antitumor immune responses.

items.title: Priming anti-tumor immunity via nutritional adjuvant therapy: A mathematical modeling and virtual cohort study regarding metabolic competition.
items.abstract: Although immunotherapy has revolutionized cancer treatment, its efficacy is frequently constrained by the metabolically hostile tumor microenvironment (TME). An important contributor is competition for shared nutrients between rapidly proliferating tumor cells and metabolically active immune effector cells. We investigated how nutritional intervention modulates this competition to favor antitumor immunity by developing and calibrating a tumor-immune model with dynamic nutritional regulation. Combining bifurcation analysis with simulations in a heterogeneous virtual mouse cohort, we compared different nutrient delivery strategies. The model predicts that nutritional regulation can generate bistability, making treatment outcomes sensitive to intervention timing and initial conditions. At the same cumulative dose, a larger initial nutrient input followed by gradual tapering produced better tumor control than constant infusion. The simulations suggest that the larger initial input accelerates T cell expansion, allowing the immune response to reduce tumor burden before nutrient delivery declines. This work provides a quantitative framework for studying nutritional modulation of tumor-immune dynamics and supports further investigation of temporally optimized nutrient delivery as an adjunct to cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: Real‑world effectiveness of neoadjuvant pembrolizumab in triple‑negative breast cancer: a retrospective case series.
items.abstract: Real-world implementation of neoadjuvant pembrolizumab in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) may be challenging in resource-constrained settings. We evaluated the real-world effectiveness of neoadjuvant pembrolizumab and explored factors associated with pathological response and early relapse-free survival (RFS) in a North African cohort. This retrospective single-center study included 33 consecutive patients with non-metastatic TNBC treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy combined with pembrolizumab between 2023 and 2025. Clinical, pathological, and treatment-related variables, including pembrolizumab exposure, treatment delays, and chemotherapy backbone, were analyzed. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response (pCR). RFS was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. The median age was 48 years, and 90.9% of patients had stage II-III disease. The pCR rate was 33.3% (11/33). Smaller baseline tumor size was significantly associated with pCR (median, 27.0 vs. 30.5mm; p=0.036). No statistically significant association was observed between pCR and pembrolizumab exposure, treatment delays, chemotherapy backbone, or other examined clinicopathological factors. RCB-0, RCB-I, RCB-II, and RCB-III were observed in 15.2%, 18.2%, 30.3%, and 36.4% of patients, respectively. After a median follow-up of 11 months, the estimated 1-year RFS was approximately 72%. No relapse was observed among patients achieving pCR, whereas the 1-year RFS was not reported separately for pCR-negative patients in this revised version. Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab demonstrated a pCR rate of 33.3% in this real-world Tunisian cohort. Given the small sample size, heterogeneous treatment exposure, and short follow-up, treatment-related and survival findings should be considered exploratory. Optimizing access and treatment continuity may be important for improving the implementation of neoadjuvant immunotherapy in resource-limited settings. Larger prospective studies are warranted to evaluate treatment delivery and long-term outcomes.

items.title: Tissue and blood-based biomarkers of immunotherapy response in head and neck Cancer.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment landscape of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). In the recurrent/metastatic (R/M) setting, pembrolizumab has been approved as first-line therapy, either alone for tumors with PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS) ≥ 1 or in combination with platinum-based chemotherapy regardless of PD-L1 CPS status. Moreover, both pembrolizumab and nivolumab have been approved as monotherapy in platinum-refractory disease. More recently, perioperative pembrolizumab received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval for resectable, locally advanced HNSCC with PD-L1 CPS ≥ 1 following encouraging results of the KEYNOTE-689 trial. Although PD-L1 CPS is the only validated HNSCC-specific biomarker for immunotherapy selection, its accuracy remains limited, as response rates are modest even among PD-L1 CPS-high patients, while some tumors with low/negative CPS may still derive benefit. This underscores the need for novel biomarkers with greater predictive value that can serve as more precise selection and risk stratification tools for patients with HNSCC considering immunotherapy. Recent studies have investigated several biomarkers of immunotherapy outcomes in HNSCC in both tissue and blood, paving the way toward adopting non-invasive approaches. In this review, we aim to summarize recent advances in ICI biomarker discovery in non-nasopharyngeal HNSCC and to set the basis for the adoption of an integrated approach, comprising both tissue-based and liquid biomarkers.

items.title: Prevalence of autoimmune hepatitis in patients with Sjögren disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Sjögren disease (SjD) and autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) may coexist, but the prevalence of AIH in SjD patients is unclear. This study investigated the prevalence and association. Databases (Web of Science, Cochrane, Embase, PubMed, CNKI, Wanfang, CBMdisc, VIP) were searched up to November 14, 2025. Quality was assessed using NOS and JBI scales. Meta-analysis was performed with R 4.5.2 (PROSPERO: CRD420251233495). Fourteen studies (3697 SjD patients) were included. Overall prevalence of AIH in SjD was 2.55% (95% CI: 1.52%-4.26%). Prevalence varied by study type (retrospective cohort: 4.58%, cross-sectional: 1.72%, prospective cohort: 1.67%) and by country (China: 6.16%, Japan: 2.51%, Spain: 2.49%). Stratified by SjD diagnostic criteria (1993 European, 2002 AECG) and AIH scoring (1993 IAIHG), prevalence was approximately 2%. Prevalence of AIH in SjD patients varies significantly by study design and region. Early diagnosis and treatment of AIH may improve quality of life and prognosis in SjD patients. This meta-analysis provides the first pooled estimate regarding the prevalence of autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) in patients with Sjögren disease (SjD): 2.55% (95% CI 1.52%-4.26%; 14 studies, 3697 patients). Subgroup analyses indicated that AIH prevalence was influenced by study design, whereas estimates stratified by SjD and AIH diagnostic criteria were of similar magnitude (approximately 2%). Regional estimates showed numerical differences, but the differences were not statistically significant; the numerically higher estimates may reflect differences in genetic susceptibility, selection bias, environmental factors, and medical screening strategies, as well as referral and detection bias. Given the observational and largely cross-sectional design of the included studies, these estimates only motivate a hypothesis-generating immunometabolic framework, rather than permitting causal or mechanistic inference. In this framework, the liver may serve as a source of autoantigens through modifications of oxidation, glycosylation, and lipidation, including the hepatocyte β2GPI-PON1 axis; this mechanism remains to be tested in the SjD-AIH overlap.

items.title: Low public awareness of hepatocellular carcinoma risk factors.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) prevention can be mediated through hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination, hepatitis C virus (HCV) treatment, and alcohol control. We assessed public awareness of their carcinogenic risks and association with digital information seeking behaviors. We analyzed the nationally representative 2024 Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS 7), including 6,711, 6,661, and 6,793 respondents with observed HBV, HCV, and alcohol awareness outcomes, respectively. Survey-weighted logistic regression with multiple imputation of missing covariates assessed associations with sociodemographic characteristics and digital behaviors. Overall awareness was low: only 18.0%, 16.7%, and 37.1% recognized HBV, HCV, and alcohol as carcinogenic, respectively. Older age was independently associated with lower alcohol-related awareness; compared with adults aged 18-34 years, those aged 35-49 years (aOR 0.67, 95% CI 0.48-0.93), 50-64 years (aOR 0.56, 95% CI 0.40-0.78), and ≥65 years (aOR 0.49, 95% CI 0.36-0.68) had lower awareness. Higher educational attainment was associated with greater alcohol-related awareness (aOR 1.86, 95% CI 1.47-2.34). Online health information seeking was associated with greater awareness of HCV-related (aOR 1.74, 95% CI 1.17-2.59) and alcohol-related cancer risk (aOR 1.95, 95% CI 1.44-2.63), but not HBV-related cancer risk (aOR 1.40, 95% CI 0.95-2.08). However, social media use was not independently associated with risk awareness in multivariable models. Public awareness of HCC risk factors remains low. General social media use was not independently associated with cancer-risk awareness, whereas online health information seeking was associated with greater HCV- and alcohol-related awareness. These findings highlight opportunities for more targeted, literacy-sensitive HCC-prevention communication. Public awareness that hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, and alcohol consumption are associated with cancer risk remains low among U.S. adults. Using nationally representative HINTS 7 data, we identified sociodemographic differences in awareness and found that general social media use was not independently associated with awareness after multivariable adjustment, whereas online health information seeking was associated with greater awareness of HCV- and alcohol-related cancer risk. These findings highlight opportunities for targeted, literacy-sensitive communication strategies that facilitate access to credible health information and strengthen HCC prevention efforts.

items.title: Comparative risk of hepatocellular carcinoma among people with chronic hepatitis B treated with tenofovir or entecavir: A population-based linkage study.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence and mortality are rising in Australia and globally. Antiviral therapies entecavir (ETV) and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) are widely used to treat chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and reduce HCC risk, but uncertainty persists regarding their relative HCC prevention impact. This study characterises HCC incidence among people with CHB treated with ETV or TDF, including sub-populations recommended for HCC surveillance. We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study in New South Wales, Australia, using linked public health datasets: 10,698 people with CHB were eligible after receiving at least 12 months of stable antiviral therapy with ETV (n=7,139) or TDF (n=3,559). Follow-up occurred from 2007-2022. Crude annual incidence rates and adjusted Cox proportional hazard ratios were calculated for HCC. Median follow-up was 86.3 months, including 89.2 months and 82.3 months among participants receiving TDF and ETV, respectively. During follow-up, 300 (2.8%) participants were diagnosed with HCC, an incidence of 4.12 per 1000 person years. Participants treated with TDF had a lower hazard ratio for HCC (aHR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.46-0.82) compared to those treated with ETV. Baseline variables associated with increased HCC risk were older age (reference <50 years: 50-59 years aHR: 2.15, 95% CI: 1.45-3.18; 60-69 years aHR: 3.42, 95% CI: 2.38-4.91; 70-79 years aHR: 4.28, 95% CI: 2.89-6.34; ≥80 years aHR: 3.95, 95% CI: 2.51-6.22), male sex (aHR: 3.14; 95% CI: 2.31-4.25), alcohol use disorder (aHR: 2.33; 95% CI: 1.28-4.25), and history of decompensated cirrhosis (aHR: 2.28; 95% CI: 1.27-4.07). In people with chronic hepatitis B in Australia on stable antiviral therapy hepatocellular carcinoma risk was lower among those receiving entecavir than those receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, although confounding remains a potential explanation. Comparative HCC risk between entecavir and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) in chronic hepatitis B remains uncertain outside East Asian cohorts. This population-based linkage study of people with chronic hepatitis B in Australia found TDF was associated with lower HCC risk than entecavir, a finding relevant to clinicians and researchers working on HCC prevention. These results support consideration of TDF as a preferred antiviral where clinically appropriate and highlight the need for HCC screening guidelines to account for treatment status alongside established risk factors such as older age and alcohol use disorder. As treatment was not randomised and residual confounding could not be completely mitigated, further prospective studies are needed to confirm this association.

items.title: Hepatitis C Elimination in Latin America: Progress, Disparities, and Lessons for the Next Phase of Liver Health.
items.abstract: In 2016, the World Health Organization set goals to eliminate the hepatitis C virus (HCV) as a public health threat by 2030; these include a 90% reduction in new infections, a 65% reduction in HCV-related mortality, the diagnosis of 90% of infected individuals, and the treatment of 80% of those eligible. Although direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) make a viral cure technically achievable, progress in Latin America remains heterogeneous. In this structured narrative review and country-level policy mapping, we assess the current epidemiology of HCV, screening and diagnostic pathways, care models, access to DAAs, national guidelines, and surveillance capabilities in select Latin American countries. While formal elimination commitments are becoming more common, universal or expanded screening, reflex diagnostic pathways, decentralized care, and integrated longitudinal registries remain unevenly implemented. Persistent deficiencies are particularly relevant for people who inject drugs (PWID), incarcerated populations, migrants, and other groups with barriers to conventional care. International experience supports point-of-care and reflex testing, prison-based testing and treatment, harm reduction integration, and decentralization as strategies to close these gaps. After achieving a sustained virological response, elimination programs must also address residual fibrosis, hepatocellular carcinoma risk, metabolic and alcohol-related liver injury, and the risk of HCV reinfection in populations that remain exposed to the virus.

items.title: Evolution of bilirubin detection: analytical strategies, sensing platforms, and translational opportunities.
items.abstract: Liver diseases, including fatty liver disease, viral hepatitis, cirrhosis, and cholestatic disorders, leading to hyperbilirubinemia contribute substantially to the global burden of morbidity and mortality. It is also a major clinical concern in neonates, with neonatal jaundice occurring in approximately 60% of term and 80% of preterm newborns during the first week after birth. Over the past decades, bilirubin detection has evolved from conventional laboratory-based methods to advanced sensing technologies designed for rapid, sensitive, and decentralized analysis. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the evolution of bilirubin sensing, with emphasis on well-established electrochemical and optical sensing to integrated paper-based, smartphone-assisted, and wearable sensor technologies. Recent advances in functional materials, miniaturized sensors, digital analysis, and integrated sensing platforms have expanded the potential for portable bilirubin testing across diverse diagnostic and monitoring settings. These advances hold promise for applications in point-of-care (POC) testing, resource-limited settings, and neonatal care units, where timely and accessible bilirubin assessment is essential for informed clinical decision-making. Established bilirubin-sensing techniques and emerging technologies are critically evaluated to highlight novel approaches, compare analytical performance, and assess translational potential. Alternative sample matrices, which offer considerable potential for diverse applications, are also evaluated to distinguish exploratory demonstrations from clinically validated applications. Furthermore, matrix effects, sensor drift, storage stability, reproducibility, and variations across devices and fabrication batches are critically examined in relation to their implications for measurement reliability and clinical applicability. By integrating advances in sensing mechanisms, functional materials, and device architectures, the discussion provides a foundation for understanding bilirubin-sensing principles, critically evaluating reported approaches, and addressing existing challenges, while offering insights into sensor design and technology selection and identifying key priorities for developing reliable, accessible, and clinically translatable bilirubin-sensing platforms.

items.title: CXCL16-CXCR6 axis drives the enrichment of CCR8 + effector regulatory T cells and shapes an immunosuppressive microenvironment in the colorectal cancer liver metastatic niche.
items.abstract: The mechanisms underlying regulatory T cell (Treg) enrichment and immunosuppressive activity in colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM) remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell transcriptomic analysis with experimental and tissue-based validation to investigate Treg heterogeneity and its potential regulation in CRLM. Our findings revealed a shift toward effector Treg states in metastatic lesions, characterized by increased CCR8 expression and associated with an immunosuppressive landscape. CellChat analysis identified CXCL16-CXCR6 as a candidate signaling axis between myeloid or dendritic populations and effector Tregs. In vitro chemotaxis assays demonstrated preferential migration of CCR8 + Tregs toward CXCL16, and this response was attenuated by CXCR6 blockade. Analyses of human CRLM cohorts and tissue samples further linked CCR8 + effector Treg enrichment to reduced effector T-cell abundance and increased inhibitory-checkpoint expression. Collectively, these findings implicate CXCL16-CXCR6-mediated chemotaxis in the accumulation of effector Tregs with immunosuppressive features in CRLM and highlight CCR8 as a marker of these Treg states, providing insight into the interplay between CXCL16-expressing myeloid populations and Tregs in the metastatic liver microenvironment.

items.title: Analysis of Toll-like receptor 3 variants in epithelial cells reveals functional independence from proteolytic cleavage in loop 1.
items.abstract: TLR3 is a pattern recognition receptor recognizing dsRNA. We investigated the functional impact of naturally occurring TLR3 single nucleotide variants (SNVs) associated with severe viral diseases on TLR3 activation and signaling upon ectopic expression in epithelial cells. Some SNVs (namely, 360P, P680L, G743S, and R811S) consistently reduced TLR3 signaling upon poly(polyinosine-polycytidylic acid) stimulation in the liver- and lung-derived Huh7.5 and A549 cells, with, in part, variable effect size. In contrast, L199F, L297V, L412F, F459L, P554S, L742F, and R867Q had no or only mild effects on TLR3 function, whereas N284I and F303S increased TLR3 activation. Notably, SNVs affecting TLR3 activation did not alter its subcellular localization or surface expression. Several SNVs that did not affect TLR3 activation had reduced proteolytic cleavage in loop 1, which was reported previously to be required for function. In contrast, we found that a cleavage-resistant TLR3 mutant was fully functional, localized to endosomes, interacted with the adapter protein TRIF, and induced IFN-stimulated genes. Importantly, protease inhibitor treatment of liver-derived PH5CH8 cells, endogenously expressing TLR3, abrogated TLR3 cleavage without affecting TLR3 function. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that SNVs may contribute to pathogenesis by impairing TLR3 signaling and that TLR3 does not require proteolytic processing for function in epithelial cell lines.

items.title: Telitacicept for Antibody-Mediated Rejection in Kidney Transplantation: A Retrospective Real-World Study.
items.abstract: Antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) remains a leading cause of late kidney allograft loss due to a lack of effective therapies. Telitacicept, a recombinant TACI-Ig fusion protein neutralizing B-lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS) and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL), showed efficacy in antibody-mediated autoimmune disorders, but its role in AMR remains unexplored. In this single-center, retrospective, real-world study, ten kidney transplant recipients with biopsy-proven active or chronic active AMR received telitacicept for ≥ 6 months plus standard antirejection therapy and underwent follow-up biopsy within one year. Outcomes included allograft function, proteinuria, donor-specific antibody (DSA) levels, and Banff scores. Over a follow-up lasting more than two years, allograft function remained stable (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] change within ±20%) in 70% (7/10), with annualized eGFR slopes ranging from -3.59 to +9.34 mL/min/1.73 m²/year among responders. Four of six patients with baseline proteinuria (>1 g/24h) had sustained reductions, and serum immunoglobulins (IgG, IgM, IgA) declined significantly (P < 0.05). Circulating human leukocyte antigen (HLA) and DSA levels generally decreased at first follow-up, with variable rebound after discontinuation. Follow-up biopsies showed reductions in intimal arteritis (v), peritubular capillaritis (ptc), and C4d deposition. Five patients no longer met Banff AMR criteria. Residual microvascular inflammation persisted in four, and borderline T-cell-mediated rejection features occurred in one. Microvascular inflammation score decreased numerically (3.5 to 2.0; P = 0.063), and chronic lesions remained largely stable. Infectious complications occurred but resolved with treatment. In this small, uncontrolled cohort, telitacicept-based therapy was associated with heterogeneous clinical and histopathological changes, warranting prospective controlled trials.

items.title: Protocol for establishing a 3D coculture of colorectal cancer liver metastasis patient-derived organoids, endothelial cells, and fibroblasts.
items.abstract: Here, we present a protocol to investigate tumor-endothelial interactions and endothelial plasticity. We describe steps for establishing patient-derived organoids (PDOs) from colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRCLM) specimens and their coculture with endothelial cells (ECs) and fibroblasts (FBs) in a three-dimensional (3D) fibrin-Matrigel hydrogel. We then detail procedures for coculture preparation, histological processing, and immunofluorescence analyses.
